Only falls through to openPath(cwd, withBundleID:) (or bare `open -b` with no path) when the app isn't running yet, so an already-open window is always focused instead of a duplicate being spawned.

Known host maps via hostBundleIDs; an unknown NON-EMPTY host that is itself the bundle ID of a RUNNING app resolves to itself (fixes every untabled editor at once, no bundle-ID guessing); only a genuinely unplaceable host (a TERM_PROGRAM value, never a bundle ID) falls back. bugs.error_message: Panel header showed '! expired' (claiming the usage auth token had died) for ANY poll failure — a dropped connection, an HTTP 5xx, or a parse failure — while the hover tooltip contradicted it with the real cause.
bugs.root_cause: UsagePoller has separate onAuthExpired and onError callbacks, but both wrote into one stringly-typed `usageError: String?`, and usageNotice mapped `usageError != nil` -> "expired". The distinction the poller made was discarded at the boundary. Compounding it, usageError was only cleared by a SUCCESSFUL poll, so turning polling off while an error showed pinned the notice in the header forever.
bugs.fix: Replaced usageError with a `UsageFailure` enum (.authExpired -> "expired", .transient(msg) -> "error"), each owning its own notice word and tooltip detail. stopPolling() now clears usageFailure, since a 'usage isn't refreshing' notice is meaningless once nothing is polling. Test locks the two words apart.

bugs.error_message: run.sh swiftc fallback: "claude spinner/MenuContentView.swift:45:46: error: cannot find 'SetupInstaller' in scope" — the non-Xcode build path could not compile at all.
bugs.root_cause: The fallback listed three source paths literally (FeedWatcher/MenuContentView/claude_spinnerApp). SetupInstaller.swift was added during the first-run-installer work and auto-joined the Xcode target — 'claude spinner/' is a SYNCHRONIZED ROOT GROUP, so new files need no pbxproj edit — but the hand-kept list in run.sh rotted silently behind that. Invisible in practice because a machine with full Xcode always takes the xcodebuild branch; only a CommandLineTools-only machine hits the fallback. Found accidentally while verifying split commits with the same three-file command.
bugs.fix: Glob instead of a literal list: swiftc -O -o claude-spinner "claude spinner"/*.swift — matches the synchronized-root-group behavior so the next new source can't break it the same way. Verified the fallback now produces an 844K binary.
